claims.text: \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has integral Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution preserving Littlewood–Richardson multiplication under conjugation. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]

groundings.excerpt:
213: Let $\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a ${\mathbb Z}$-linear basis consisting of \emph{Schur functions} $s_{\lambda}$,
214: where $\lambda$ is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
215: \[I_{r,n-r} = \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{s_\lambda\mid \lambda\nsubseteq (n-r)^r \right\} \]
216: of $\Lambda$. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
217: \[H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. \]
218: We will use an overline to denote the projection $\Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. Specifically, we will write $\overline{\Lambda}$ as a shorthand for $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. We will also distinguish between $s_{\lambda}\in \Lambda$, the usual Schur function, and $\overline{s}_{\lambda}$ for its image in $\overline{\Lambda}$.

claims.text: For the conjugate non-self-conjugate inputs \([222,4^5]\subseteq\Lambda/I_{5,4}\) and \([33,5^4]\subseteq\Lambda/I_{4,5}\), complete \(A_+J\)-relation matrices and quotient Smith data in degrees \(6,\ldots,20\) agree: free-rank sequence \((1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)\) and no torsion in either case. [artifact 5b6e59b74af1b386568e8d3014cdef276ec80f89225cf5ba2367c73fa3b0a993]

Conditional on the accepted ideal correspondence \(\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\), conjugation induces a graded integral isomorphism \[ J_v/A_+J_v\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}. \] Consequently it preserves every degreewise torsion subgroup and free rank.
